meta.title: Who really said "I can't believe how fast 20 years went by... Mamba Out!"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Kobe Bryant really said it — both halves, at Staples Center on 13 April 2016. But the ellipsis hides his entire farewell speech in between.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'I can't believe how fast 20 years went by... Mamba Out!'?
meta.ogDescription: Verified: Kobe Bryant's farewell speech, 13 April 2016. The line splices the speech's opening words to its closing 'What can I say? Mamba out.'

answer.label: Spoken by
answer.sourceLine: Both halves are real, and both come from the same night: Bryant’s unscripted farewell to the crowd at Staples Center after his final NBA game on 13 April 2016. The catch is the ellipsis — “I can’t believe how fast 20 years went by” opened the speech, “Mamba Out!” ended it, and everything he actually said in between has been swallowed by three dots.
answer.confidenceText: Verified — but it is a splice of the speech’s first line and its last.

source.heading: The source

docMeta.dd: Farewell speech after his final NBA game
Broadcast video; transcribed by Wikiquote and news outlets

source.excerpt: I can’t believe how fast 20 years went by. I mean, this is crazy… To be standing here, standing on the court with my teammates behind me, and appreciate this journey that we’ve been along… What can I say? Mamba Out!
trail: Wikiquote’s sourced Quotes section ↗ prints a block beginning “I can’t believe how fast 20 years went by. I mean, this is crazy…” and ending “What can I say? Mamba Out!”, cited to video of the speech after Bryant’s last game, 13 April 2016.

ESPN’s game report ↗ puts both halves in Bryant’s mouth that night: “I can’t believe how fast 20 years went by. Man, this is crazy” and, as his closing statement, “What can I say? Mamba out.” It dates the game to 13 April 2016 and records 60 points in a 101–96 win over Utah.

Independent transcripts confirm the ordering: Speakola ↗ opens the speech with the “twenty years” line and closes it with “What can I say, Mamba out,” and IBTimes’ transcript ↗ likewise ends on that line. The two clauses in the popular quote are therefore the first and last things he said.
The primary artifact still exists: NBA on ESPN’s video of the speech ↗ is the recording Wikiquote cites, so the wording can be checked against the delivery rather than against another transcript.
source.excerptNote: The ellipses stand in for most of the address — his memories of growing up a Lakers fan, the joke about twenty years of fans yelling “pass the ball!”, and his thanks to Vanessa, Natalia and Gianna.

author.name: Kobe Bryant
author.heading: About Kobe Bryant
author.bio: Kobe Bean Bryant was born in Philadelphia on 23 August 1978 and drafted straight out of high school in 1996 — taken 13th overall by the Charlotte Hornets and immediately traded to the Los Angeles Lakers, where he spent his entire twenty-year professional career. He was widely regarded as one of the greatest basketball players of all time, and after retiring he won an Academy Award in 2018 for the animated short Dear Basketball. He died in a helicopter crash in Calabasas, California on 26 January 2020, aged 41.

misattribution.heading: Not misattributed — miscut
misattribution.intro: Nobody else is credited with this line, and no one needs to be: Kobe Bryant said every word of it. What the popular version gets wrong is not who but how — three dots doing an enormous amount of work.

items.why: The two clauses are not consecutive. Full transcripts show “I can’t believe how fast 20 years went by” as the speech’s opening line and “Mamba out” as its last words ↗, with the thanks to fans, teammates and family in between.

He actually said “What can I say? Mamba out.” ↗ The popular version drops the shrug that sets up the drop. Outlets also punctuate the sign-off differently — ESPN prints “Mamba out.”, Wikiquote “Mamba Out!” — so the exclamation mark is a transcription choice, not a settled fact.
Because the speech was unscripted and transcribed by ear, outlets differ on what followed: ESPN prints “Man, this is crazy,” while Sports Illustrated prints “It’s crazy. It’s absolutely crazy.” ↗
Some transcript pages head the speech 14 April, the date of next-morning coverage. ESPN dates the game and the speech to Wednesday night, 13 April 2016 ↗.

misattribution.truthLine: Genuine, and genuinely his: Wikiquote’s sourced entry prints the same opening and closing words inside a longer, ellipsis-condensed block ↗, cited to video of the 13 April 2016 farewell — and the popular version compresses that block much further. Read it as a condensation of a whole speech, not a single sentence.

context.heading: The night the mic dropped
lead: On the evening of 13 April 2016, in the last game of a twenty-season career spent entirely with the Los Angeles Lakers, Kobe Bryant scored 60 points and the Lakers came from behind to beat the Utah Jazz 101–96. He took 50 shots to get there. Then, still in his sweat-soaked No. 24 jersey, he was handed a microphone at centre court.

What followed was not a written speech. It rambled, doubled back, and got laughs — he cracked up over spending twenty years hearing fans yell “pass the ball!” only for them to spend his last night yelling the opposite. It thanked the fans, the organisation, his teammates, his wife Vanessa and his daughters. And it ended with four words and a literal mic drop.
context.detailsSummary: Why the quote travels as a splice
detailsBody: The two clauses that circulate together are the bookends of the address. Wikiquote condenses the speech too, but nothing like as hard: its sourced entry keeps six passages joined by five ellipses, where the popular version leaves one pair of clauses and a single set of dots standing for everything else. That is what turns a rambling, grateful, funny farewell into what looks like a single crisp aphorism about time passing.

It also quietly drops the four words that actually preceded the sign-off. What he said was “What can I say? Mamba out.” The shrug is part of the moment; the meme version cuts the shrug and keeps the exclamation mark.
context.pull: You can’t write something better than this.

sourcesVerified.claim: Wikiquote's sourced Quotes section carries the quotation beginning "I can't believe how fast 20 years went by. I mean, this is crazy…" and ending "What can I say? Mamba Out!", cited to "A speech after Bryant's last game, 13 April 2016, posted on YouTube." The page also gives his dates as born 23 August 1978, died 26 January 2020, and describes a 20-year career entirely with the Lakers.

ESPN's report dates Bryant's final NBA game to Wednesday night, 13 April 2016, a 101–96 Lakers win over the Utah Jazz in which he scored 60 points, and quotes "I can't believe how fast 20 years went by. Man, this is crazy," "You can't write something better than this," and the closing "What can I say? Mamba out."

Speakola's transcript of the last-game speech opens "Man, I can't believe how fast twenty years went by" and concludes "What can I say, Mamba out," at Staples Center, Los Angeles (the page heads it 14 April 2016).

IBTimes India's printed transcript of the farewell speech runs through the die-hard-Lakers-fan passage, the "pass the ball" joke and the thanks to Vanessa, and ends on the final line "What can I say, Mamba out."

Sports Illustrated's contemporaneous piece quotes the speech as "I can't believe how fast 20 years went by. It's crazy. It's absolutely crazy," references "Mamba out," and dates the final game to 13 April 2016 (Lakers 101, Jazz 96, 60 points on 50 shots).
The video is titled "'Mamba out' - Remembering Kobe Bryant's farewell speech after his last NBA game (2016)" on the NBA on ESPN channel — the recording Wikiquote cites as its source.

Wikipedia gives Kobe Bryant's birth as 23 August 1978 in Philadelphia, death 26 January 2020 in Calabasas aged 41, position shooting guard, career 1996–2016 spent entirely with the Los Angeles Lakers, drafted 13th overall in 1996 by the Charlotte Hornets and traded to the Lakers, and notes his 2018 Academy Award for Dear Basketball.

TSN's retrospective dates the final game to 13 April 2016, records the 101–96 win over Utah with 60 points on 22-of-50 shooting, describes Bryant addressing the crowd in his sweat-soaked No. 24 jersey, and gives the closing line as "What can I say? Mamba out" followed by a mic drop.
